qa.text: The four levels read right to a leader who has never used an agent, and each one builds on the one before
The request queue plan in Level 3 is true to how triage works, with no employer or real request in it
The task planner on your phone: start from an example or your own task, add parts from the two shelves, see the level it reaches and what it is missing, then Save the plan file and open it
The page reads plain and to the point, with the recipe language gone: the opening, the rules section and Level 2 aloud
The section on why a prompt is a workflow, and its table lining up the two vocabularies, make the case to a leader
The section on where a rule is enough, and its rules beside AI with a check, make the case
The five redrawn figures read on your phone and at your desk, night and day: the vocabulary table, rules beside AI, the four levels, the numbered prompt, the loop
The new section on measuring whether it works reads right to a leader: the baseline at level 1, a small pilot, the four counts in the table, and the check as the balancing measure
Using AI to think a problem through (end of Level 2): the Monday example prompt and the advice to ask for the case against your plan
Facts apart from guesses at Level 2: the paragraph, line 6 of the numbered prompt, the worked plan, and the new part and baseline field in the task planner
